implementation_notes: A ScopedValue is an implicit method parameter with a bounded lifetime: where(KEY, v).run(() -> ...) binds the value for the execution of the lambda, every callee reads it with KEY.get(), and the binding reverts when run returns - including nested rebinding for a sub-scope. It is one-way (there is no set), which is exactly the provider/reader split, and bindings are inherited by child threads started with StructuredTaskScope. Prefer it over ThreadLocal whenever the goal is one-way transmission of request context.
pitfalls: get() on an unbound ScopedValue throws - guard with isBound() or orElse/orElseThrow instead of assuming a default.
Only StructuredTaskScope child threads inherit bindings; a task handed to a plain executor or a new Thread does not, and its callees see an unbound value.
The value must be immutable or access-synchronised, and scoped values are designed to be used in small numbers: many of them defeat the per-thread cache the JDK relies on.

variants.name: ThreadLocal carrier (pre-25, mutable per-thread value)
variants.idiom_name: static final ThreadLocal<T> with explicit remove() (InheritableThreadLocal for child threads)
variants.implementation_notes: The classic JVM mechanism: a static final ThreadLocal is set by the request-handling code and read anywhere below it on the same thread, with InheritableThreadLocal for values that must reach child threads. The JDK's own rationale for ScopedValue lists its defects - any callee can set() it, its lifetime is unbounded, and inheritance copies the whole thread-local map per child thread - so use it when targeting pre-25 runtimes, for genuinely per-thread state such as caches, or when a value must be mutated from below.
pitfalls: Forgetting remove() in a finally block retains the value for the life of the thread and leaks it into the next request on a pooled thread.
Nothing prevents a faraway callee from calling set(), turning one-way context into spaghetti state flow across the call stack.
InheritableThreadLocal copies every thread-local in the parent at thread creation, which is expensive once virtual threads or large pools are involved.
